articles.authors: Scott Madaras, Alex Sarracino, Morgann Berg, Wilfredo Cabrera, Michael Busse, Andrew Pomerene, Andrew Starbuck, Matt Boady, Nathan Young, Michael J. Abere, Christopher Long
articles.summary: We demonstrate a scalable post-fabrication trimming technique for silicon photonic devices utilizing a germanium-doped silicon dioxide (SiO2:Ge) cladding sensitive to ultraviolet femtosecond laser irradiation. Precise refractive index tuning is essential to compensate for fabrication-induced variations in large-scale integrated photonic circuits, enabling improved device performance without active power consumption. By irradiating SiO2:Ge films with 258-nm, 400-fs pulses, we achieve controllable, permanent refractive index shifts (Δn > 0.06) that exceed prior laser trimming results by over an order of magnitude at substantially lower cumulative doses. …

articles.authors: Qilin Sun, Yang Liu, Qingqing Cen, Yue Han, Ying Shang, Gang Ma, Pinru Wu
articles.summary: Introduction Facial aging in Asian populations presents unique challenges, as photoaging frequently coexists with melasma, and conventional laser treatments carry elevated post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH) risk. The comparative efficacy of different 755-nm picosecond alexandrite laser (PSAL) delivery systems remains unclear. This study aims to compare the efficacy and safety of 755-nm PSAL flat optic versus diffractive lens array (DLA) for facial rejuvenation in Chinese women with Fitzpatrick skin types III-IV and melasma. Methods This randomized split-face trial enrolled 80 Chinese women with symmetrical facial photoaging and melasma. …

SEM, AFM, particle statistics, and textural anisotropy analysis revealed fluence-dependent morphological regimes. …

articles.summary: Grating-assisted space-division phase-shifting incoherent digital holography (IDH) allows a conventional image sensor to simultaneously record multiple phase-shifted holograms, enabling single-shot acquisition of complex-amplitude information. However, conventional binary grating configurations involve a trade-off between high diffraction efficiency and uniform optical-power distribution among the phase-shifted holograms. To address this issue, we propose a multilevel two-dimensional phase grating that generates four principal diffraction orders with high and nearly equal efficiencies. …

articles.authors: Daniel Holder, Matthias Buser, Rudolf Weber, Volkher Onuseit, Thomas Graf
articles.summary: Achieving “first time right” depth precision in volumetric laser ablation – particularly for deep features exceeding 50 μm – is challenging due to dynamic effects such as incubation-induced changes in ablation efficiency and altered laser-material coupling caused by the formation of Laser-Induced Periodic Surface Structures (LIPSS). This work presents an industrial-grade setup for closed-loop volumetric ablation that integrates an ultrafast laser, a galvanometer scanner, and coaxial Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) for real-time depth control. …

articles.summary: We exploited the surface-modified laser-induced graphene (LIG) resistors decorated with gold, silver, or platinum nanoparticles (AuNPs, AgNPs, or PtNPs) to reduce their low-frequency noise. The resistors can be used to prepare sensors or contact paths in wearable electronics due to their elastic properties, and their inherent noise impacts their performance. The simple NPs modification of the LIG surface resulted in a noise-reduction effect, which increased in the following order: Pt<Ag<Au for the devices investigated here.​ Au-decorated LIG exhibited a 32-times reduction of normalized voltage noise. …

articles.title: Ion-Access Engineering for High-Performance Vertical Organic Electrolyte-Gated Transistors
articles.authors: Wang J, Teuerle L, Chen L, Meier T, Sun T, Antrack T, Dong T, Zhang Z, Li P, Weissbach A, Solgi A, Kleemann H
institutions: Center of Smart Materials and Devices
articles.summary: Organic electrolyte-gated transistors (OEGTs) are promising platforms for bioelectronics and neuromorphic systems owing to their low-voltage operation and strong ionic-electronic coupling. However, in vertical OEGTs, which offer higher current densities and faster switching, the semiconductor channel is often shielded from direct electrolyte contact, limiting ionic accessibility and resulting in inefficient gate coupling and slow switching dynamics. Here, we introduce a photolithography-free ion-access strategy for vertical OEGTs, combining femtosecond laser micropatterning with inkjet-printed solid-state electrolytes. …

articles.title: High-resolution dual-layer two-photon lithography for nanoscale patterning
articles.authors: Chenran Zhang, Yun‐Lu Sun, Zifeng Xiao, Xiuzhen Xu, Xiaobin Xu
articles.summary: Multi-photon lithography (MPL), which predominantly utilises femtosecond lasers, is a significant maskless, high-resolution and ambient (non-vacuum) lithography technique. To achieve a comparable resolution to primary competing solutions, such as electron-beam lithography, and to improve processing efficiency or throughput, the implementation of costly, complex methodologies is usually necessary. These include specialised material customisation, precise control over light-matter interactions, and sophisticated optical instrumentation. In this work, we introduce dual-layer two-photon lithography (DL-TPL), a new patterning approach that combines dual-layer lithography with TPL. …
